test_input: Press RIGHT, then LEFT, then DOWN repeatedly until a piece locks. Press UP to rotate. Press R to restart. Press ESCAPE to quit.
expected_win_output: No win condition in Simple Tetris (game continues until game over).
expected_lose_output: GAME OVER (printed once to the console) and final score remains visible in the top-right Score label.
notes:
Controls and console prints:
- LEFT arrow: moves piece left if possible. Console prints exactly: MOVE LEFT
- RIGHT arrow: moves piece right if possible. Console prints exactly: MOVE RIGHT
- DOWN arrow: soft drop (moves piece down one row immediately). Console prints exactly: SOFT DROP. If the piece cannot move down, it locks and a new piece spawns.
- UP arrow: rotate 90 degrees clockwise if rotation does not collide. Console prints exactly: ROTATE (only when rotation succeeds).
- R: restart the game (clears grid, resets score to 0). Console prints exactly: RESTART
- ESCAPE: quit the game. Console prints exactly: QUIT
- When the game ends due to spawn collision, the console prints: GAME OVER
HUD and visuals:
- The score is shown at the top-right at all times using the Score label (text: "Score: X").
- On game over the Game Over label (center) becomes visible showing "GAME OVER" and the score remains visible.
Gameplay notes / implementation details:
- Grid is 10 columns by 20 rows. Tile size chosen to fit 400x600 viewport (30 px tiles). Grid drawn centered horizontally.
- Only four piece shapes appear: O (square 2x2), I (line), L (L-shape), and T (T-shape). Each shape has a distinct solid color (no sprite images used).
- Pieces fall automatically at a fixed interval (drop interval 0.5s). Clearing a full horizontal row removes it, shifts above rows down, and adds 100 points per cleared line.
- Rotation that would overlap walls or locked cells is ignored.
- Restart (R) fully clears the grid and resets score to 0. Quit (Escape) closes the window immediately.
Limitations / known issues:
- No sounds or music implemented (Planner specified none).
- No hold/next preview, no score multipliers; single-line clear gives +100 per line.
- Tile size is computed to fit the viewport; if the window is resized externally the layout does not dynamically adapt (the project runs at the fixed 400x600 viewport specified in project.godot).
Files implementing behavior:
- game/main.gd: all gameplay, input, rendering, scoring and state logic.
- game/main.tscn: root scene and HUD Labels (ScoreLabel, GameOverLabel).
- game/__init__.py: empty package marker as required.
